amendments.change: §13.2 reliability validation changed from 'reviewer extracts all 30 blind' to a HYBRID design: 10 blind (clean AI-vs-human kappa/PABAK) + 20 verification (reviewer corrects AI output; field-level correction rate). The blind-verification agreement gap is reported as a measured anchoring-bias estimate. Exclusion set also widened from the 5 form-pilot papers to all 7 prior-pilot papers (5 form-pilot + 2 v2.1/v2.2 re-pilot fresh) to avoid overfitting + contamination.
amendments.rationale: Reviewer declined ~10-12 h of full blind extraction. The reviewer first proposed having AI agents do the charting, which would make the validation AI-vs-AI (circular, high by construction at temperature 0, shares model biases, cannot detect them, and violates the §0.3/§2 role declaration that forbids any AI-vs-AI agreement check). The hybrid design keeps a genuine human anchor (10 blind) while minimising reviewer effort, and quantifies the verification subset's anchoring bias rather than leaving it as an unmeasured caveat. n=10 clean kappa has wide CIs; the claim rests on the combination of blind kappa + verification correction rate + programmatic grounding check.

amendments.change: §13.2 pilot reframed explicitly as quality-control/feasibility (not certification); the quantitative Level A reliability claim moved to the audit sample, whose fraction is raised 10% -> 20%. Level B reliability explicitly rests on integral human review, not kappa.
amendments.rationale: Monte Carlo power analysis (output/power_analysis/) shows n=10-30 cannot certify a per-variable kappa: at n=10 a true kappa=0.6 yields a 95% interval [0.00, 1.00]; CI half-width 0.15 needs n~150 (balanced) to 300-500 (rare classes); rare-class variables give undefined kappa in 11-49% of n=10 samples. The thesis-central variables (level_3b, Level B continuous-process fields) are the rarest, hence worst-powered. Raising the audit to 20% buys more precision than enlarging the pilot. Reviewer chose 'power analysis first' + 'reframe QC + lean on audit' (declined 2nd reviewer and larger blind n).
amendments.effort_tradeoff: 20% of a ~200-300 provisional-accept pool is ~40-60 blind manual papers (vs the pilot's 10). This is the cost of locating the reliability claim in the audit; reviewer accepted it.

amendments.change: Validation methodology redesigned from the §13.2 hybrid (10 blind + 20 verification) pilot + random-20% audit to 'Validation Protocol C', specified authoritatively in VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_C.md. C = two-model extraction (Claude Opus 4.8 + GPT/Codex; optional current Gemini as non-binding Tier-1 arbiter) over the whole available corpus -> blind-first adjudication of ALL Tier-1 (methodological_eligibility/level_3b/paper_type/borderline) disagreements -> stratified blind audit of the concordant set (oversample continuous-process/rare classes; exhaustive concordant-3B) + adversarial false-negative hunt for Corpus B -> capture-recapture (audit x FN-hunt as two detectors, Chapman estimator) -> integral human review of all Level-3B Level-B fields. Headline metric = estimated residual charting error per variable (Wilson CI / Gwet AC1), NOT Cohen's kappa. Inter-model agreement is routing only, never a reliability metric. Schema unchanged (FROZEN v2.2.1).
amendments.rationale: Three converging inputs: (1) the power analysis killed per-variable kappa certification at sustainable n; (2) the cross-model probe (output/pilot_30/ai_blind_test/, Codex vs Claude on the 10 blind keys) showed inter-model disagreement concentrates on the consequential borderline/Corpus-B calls, making it an efficient router for human effort, while confirming agreement != correctness; (3) a multi-round red-team (REDTEAM_ROUND1.md = 3 Claude lenses; plus external GPT/Gemini reviews supplied by the reviewer) converged on: reframe as QC/error-estimation not kappa; stratified not random audit; blind-first adjudication to kill anchoring at the root; N=2 not 3; capture-recapture to bound the consensus blind spot; integral Level-B human review. The hybrid 10+20 design is superseded; its anchoring concern is now eliminated by blind-first adjudication rather than measured after the fact.

amendments.change: Protocol C revised C-1.0 -> C-2.0 (VALIDATION_PROTOCOL_C.md) after a Round-2 verified defect review + 3-designer redesign panel (REVIEW_ROUND2_C2.md). Seven surgical changes: (1) capture-recapture DELETED -> exhaustible FN candidate-union census (model flags + deterministic lexicon + counter-anchored recall pass) with lexicon-expansion closure rule; (2) stratified audit + 3 coexisting sizing rules -> SRS n=40 (seed 44) from the concordant Level-A frame, per-field exact Clopper-Pearson 95% CIs, rare consequential cells (concordant-3B, lexicon hits, borderline) censused exhaustively and excluded from the frame; (3) Tier-2 INVERTED: blind-first human extraction of all Corpus-B Level-B fields (form withholds AI pre-fill until commit; models revealed after as discrepancy checkers); (4) composite residual estimator R-hat + Gwet AC1 + 'residual~0 on adjudicated units' DELETED -> metrics reported per field/per instrument, never pooled; test-retest reviewer self-consistency check ADDED (~20-30 decisions, >=2 weeks); (5) pre-registered acceptance/escalation thresholds + effort-overrun cut order (C-2 sec 6), filed verbatim in the OSF amendment; (6) Gemini third-model arbiter DELETED; contamination probe REPLACED by the corpus-wide grounding check (sec 12.2 module); determinism canary kept (20-30 papers); (7) B-first execution order registered (FN census + Corpus-B roster locked first, blind Level-B extraction second, adjudication + audit after).
amendments.rationale: Round-2 review confirmed 6 defects in C-1.0: (1) pooled-Wilson estimator invalid under the deliberately oversampled stratified audit (audit_sampler.py implemented fraction+min-cell; the Wilson half-width fixed parameter was implemented nowhere; residual_report.py pooled naively); (2) capture-recapture detectors had mismatched error universes (keyword hunt catches only Corpus-B FNs; audit catches all classes) and n12=0 was the likely outcome, making Chapman's N-hat decorative; (3) the analytically central tier (Corpus-B Level-B) had anchored AI-pre-fill verification while less important tiers got blind-first; (4) three coexisting audit-sizing rules with no binding rule; (5) human residual error hard-coded to zero with no instrument measuring the single reviewer; (6) no pre-specified thresholds/actions. A 3-designer blind panel independently rebuilt C's operational skeleton and diverged only at the defects; the judge's verdict was 'patch C, do not redesign' (switching costs + reviewer approval + built modules).

amendments.consequence_registered_not_new: §3-Step-6 already legislates this case: a canary rerun whose application version or displayed model label differs from the original run is retained and reported but marked CONFIGURATION-NON-COMPARABLE, not presented as a fixed-configuration canary. The end-of-run ChatGPT canary therefore lands in segment 2 while 440 of 448 standing ChatGPT extractions were produced in segment 1, so the ChatGPT side of the canary is configuration-non-comparable for those papers. No new policy is created here; the registered rule is invoked. The Claude side is unaffected unless it also drifts.
amendments.why_not_a_new_run_id: The run is one continuous charting effort over one frozen corpus with one frozen prompt set; only the vendor's application build changed. Splitting run_id would fragment the batch history and the per-paper timestamps that §3-Step-1 requires to stay contiguous.
